claims.value: Toreno gives side B Albuquerque with 3,000 cavalry at Azutan to watch the fords; Bassecourt’s fifth division guards the bridge separately.
claims.rationale: Assigned guarding population, not all cavalry simultaneously engaged or a total Spanish return. English rendering (ours): "He left Bassecourt’s fifth division guarding the bridge and Albuquerque with 3,000 cavalry at Azutan to watch the fords."

claims.value: Toreno distinguishes Bassecourt’s bridge infantry and Albuquerque’s cavalry under Cuesta’s disposition.
claims.rationale: The same paragraph gives Albuquerque the ford-watch cavalry task; printed one-commander label is incomplete. English rendering (ours): "Leaving the fifth division under Luis Bassecourt to guard the bridge."

claims.value: Jourdan says Mortier directed the action while Soult made dispositions and reconnaissance the day before.
claims.rationale: Praise attributed, not validation of skill; superior and local direction distinguished. English rendering (ours): "This action did much honour to Mortier, who directed it; Soult used the next day to make dispositions and reconnoitre."

claims.value: Jourdan describes the French attack by ford and bridge against the guarded crossing.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Caulaincourt’s dragoons, covered by two voltigeur brigades, crossed the Tagus upstream at a ford."

claims.value: Jourdan describes barricades, batteries and infantry in two bridge towers.
